# ImageFilterComponent accessibility issues

Generated by accessibility-auditor. Resolve these issues before using this component in production.

## Host element with `role="img"` has no accessible name

**File:** `image-filter.component.ts` — `host: { role: 'img' }` (line 12)

**WCAG criterion:** 1.1.1 Non-text Content (Level A) and 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A)

**Problem:** The host element declares `role="img"` but neither the component nor its template provide an accessible name (`aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`). Screen readers will announce this as an unlabelled image, giving users no information about the content being presented.

**Recommendation:** Expose an `ariaLabel = input<string>()` and bind it in the host via `'[attr.aria-label]': 'ariaLabel()'`. This allows each consumer to supply a contextual label (e.g. the destination name). Alternatively, document clearly that the consumer must add `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` directly on the `<company-image-filter>` host element.

---

## Projected `<img>` creates redundant image semantics inside `role="img"`

**File:** `image-filter.component.html` (line 1) — `<ng-content select="img">` / `image-filter.component.scss` (line 22) — `::ng-deep > img { z-index: -1 }`

**WCAG criterion:** 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (Level A)

**Problem:** A native `<img>` element is projected inside a host that already carries `role="img"`. Assistive technologies encounter two overlapping image landmarks: the outer `role="img"` host and the inner native `<img>` with its own `alt` text. This causes screen readers to announce the image twice or present conflicting information to the user.

**Recommendation:** The consumer must add `aria-hidden="true"` to the projected `<img>` so that only the host's `role="img"` (with its `aria-label`) is exposed in the accessibility tree. Document this requirement clearly so that no consumer projects a visible `<img>` without suppressing it from AT.
